claims.text: High-temperature structural and chemical stability is governed by atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion.
The stability of these nanoparticles can be predicted using atomistic simulations.
The initial nanoparticles are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid solutions with an FCC crystal structure.
Molecular dynamics simulations can model nanoparticle stability and property evolution under catalytic and thermoelectric operating conditions.
The proposed simulations use a 1 fs time step and a total duration of 100 ns.
Catalytic operation is evaluated from 773 to 1173 K.
Thermoelectric operation is evaluated from 473 to 1923 K.
Atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion influence thermal stability.
Atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion influence phase transitions.
Atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion influence defect formation.
Changes in thermal stability, phase transitions, and defect formation affect catalytic properties.
Changes in thermal stability, phase transitions, and defect formation affect thermoelectric properties.
Optimized atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion will increase nanoparticle stability by 20% relative to the baseline.
Optimized atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion will improve catalytic activity by 15% at 973 K relative to the baseline.
The baseline consists of physically or chemically fabricated nanoparticles without optimized atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion.
The hypothesis applies to FCC multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles within the stated catalytic and thermoelectric temperature ranges.
Simulation accuracy depends on the choice of interatomic potential.
Simulation accuracy depends on simulation parameters.
XRD can be used to determine crystal structure and lattice parameters, while TEM can evaluate morphology and size distribution.
The hypothesis is falsified if varying atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion produces no correlation with catalytic and thermoelectric properties and less than 5% improvement.
